open_gaps: County-by-county occurrence and abundance are not mapped.
Common and native weeds beyond this catalog remain to be added; this is not the entire Colorado flora.
Some species complexes, subspecies and hybrids need expert verification; image identity follows the credited source.
Species-specific pet toxicology is missing for many plants and is labeled in each profile.
One hybrid-toadflax flower photograph is only 176 by 329 pixels.

The wild-violet genus is represented by one species, and several manufacturer topics combine species still missing from this guide. The comparison is a research backlog, not evidence that every missing plant occurs in Colorado.

source_comparison.unit: Dedicated source topic, not species count or clinical completeness. Compound and genus topics remain partial until all named components are covered.
source_comparison.scope: Only the specified finite Corteva Western Rangeland guide and CSU Weed Descriptions article; not every page on either website. Missing topics are research candidates, not confirmed Colorado occurrences.
taxonomic_notes: Conyza canadensis maps to Erigeron canadensis using the NC State species account.
The older Chrysothamnus genus topic is partly represented by Ericameria nauseosa, formerly Chrysothamnus nauseosus.
Corteva’s conflicting giant-ragweed scientific label remains unresolved in this audit, even though our guide now includes independently sourced Ambrosia trifida.
Viola spp. remains partial because Viola sororia is only one species.
Full match means a named taxon has a profile; subspecies, image and toxicology limits remain in that profile.

note: CSU mistakenly repeats Centaurea maculosa under Russian knapweed. Matched by the Russian-knapweed topic to Acroptilon/Rhaponticum repens, not merged into spotted knapweed.

A.label: A — Eradicate
A.summary: Uncommon in Colorado. All populations are designated for eradication statewide.
A.interpretation: Plain-language editorial label for a management category; not a toxicity or danger rating.

B.label: B — Stop the spread
B.summary: Established in some areas. Requirements vary by location: eradication, containment or suppression to stop further spread.
B.interpretation: Plain-language editorial label for a management category; not a toxicity or danger rating.

C.label: C — Manage widespread weeds
C.summary: Widespread and well established. Control is recommended by the state; local governments may require management.
C.interpretation: Plain-language editorial label for a management category; not a toxicity or danger rating.
